title: How GenAI Can Undermine Its Own Productivity Gains: The Role of Technological Dependencies and Human Capabilities
content: Delegating a function to generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) may produce an immediate productivity gain without securing the conditions required to sustain it. This conceptual article examines when delegation-induced changes in technological dependencies and the maintenance of human capabilities can affect subsequent productivity in the same business activity. Using theory adaptation, it combines an account of changed technological requirements with conditional antecedents concerning the organizational availability and maintenance of necessary human capabilities. The resulting proposition identifies two possible pathways: insufficient human capacity for routine evaluation, correction or exception handling despite normal GenAI service; and deterioration of a required technological contribution without adequate replacement. Either pathway affects productivity only where compensation is insufficient and the relationship between quality-consistent accepted output and predefined relevant real inputs worsens. Initial gains may persist, erode or disappear; observed productivity may also fall below its historical pre-delegation level. Such a historical reversal alone does not establish causation: erosion of the GenAI-attributable gain requires credible no-delegation comparisons for the relevant periods. Constructed comparisons illustrate these mechanisms, their boundary conditions and implications for capability maintenance and technological continuity.
